title: Waleed <> Kobi - Transcript

items.topic: November 1 go-live at risk from added scope
items.statement: Kobi said he does not know how much more time is needed or whether the November 1 go-live is realistic, because the client keeps adding scope.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I think the hard part right now is I don't know how much more time we're going to need, between now and November 1st or even if November 1st is going to be realistic based on… / Kobi Kunasekaran: where we are for go live. I don't know how much more time we need because they keep adding addition cope. So yeah. Yeah.
items.note: Internal Jumpr discussion (Waleed and Kobi only); not client-confirmed.

items.statement: Kobi said the team just finished the discovery for redeposits.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We also just finished the discovery for redeposits, too.

items.statement: Kobi said payouts is the only other big item from the original phases, and more discovery on referrals is planned for Wednesday of that week.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And the only other big thing that was in our original phases was payouts. and then we're supposed to have a more discovery on referrals on Wednesday this week.
items.note: 'Wednesday this week' relative to 2026-09-21 would be 2026-09-23 (inferred, not stated).

items.topic: Work beyond original phases is extra
items.statement: Kobi said that once payouts is done, everything in the original project scope is covered, and all other work is extra.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, if we can get the payouts out of the way too, that covers everything kind of we've started with in terms of what we were supposed to build as part of this project. And then all the other stuff is extra.
items.note: Internal Jumpr discussion (Waleed and Kobi only); not client-confirmed. Kobi's view of scope boundary; no client statement in these lines.

items.topic: Track redeposit allocations and assignments in Salesforce
items.statement: Kobi described the client's current redeposit allocation process (an external tool outputs a CSV that managers copy into rep spreadsheets; reps assign to players manually) and said creating and tracking redeposits, allocations and assignments must move into Salesforce; he said he told them Jumpr can do that.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... it spits out a CSV of every single row for the redeposit for the manager to then copy and paste into the rep's spreadsheet and then for the rep they'll go through those and assign it to the player and stuff manually. / ... Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So, we need to move the tracking into Salesforce, creating and tracking those redeposits and allocations and assignments in Salesforce. so I think that's easily doable we have to architect that solution and I said okay we can do that
items.note: Second-hand recount in an internal meeting of a client redeposit session held the same day; verify against that client transcript before treating as decided. Quote uses '...' to mark omitted spans within lines 342 and 345.

items.topic: Phase 1: keep client allocation tool, integrate via import
items.statement: Kobi proposed keeping the client's external allocation tool for now; in the first phase Salesforce feeds the tool's inputs and takes its outputs in one import that creates the redeposit rows, and managers do any manual reallocation in Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... I don't want to suggest that we move that whole thing into Salesforce yet. I'm proposing that we still keep it. ... what we can do for the first phase is make sure that Salesforce is able to feed the inputs for this website that you have and… / Kobi Kunasekaran: it's able to read the outputs that you provide. ... export and import directly to Salesforce in one import and then it creates all the rows and then it's up to the manager to then if they need to do any custom manual reallocate applications or anything like that, they can do that directly in Salesforce. So that's what I'm thinking about proposing in terms of the current version
items.note: Internal Jumpr discussion (Waleed and Kobi only); not client-confirmed. Line 345 precedes the 00:40:00 marker at line 347; its nearest preceding timestamp is outside the allowed ranges.

items.topic: Allocation logic / AI move deferred past V1
items.statement: Moving the client's redeposit allocation logic into Salesforce (Agentforce or other AI) was positioned as a later step. Waleed asked whether it should be in phase one; Kobi said it does not need to be V1 and would otherwise push past November 1, and Waleed accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: It's just a cloud prompt or whatever it is that they did, a skill. So I think we can try to figure out how to move that over to agent force or… / Waleed Alasadi: I mean fine fine but it be part of the solution for phase one or… / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think the import process we still need to build that anyways for manual overrides. That's why I'm thinking this doesn't need to be V1. / Waleed Alasadi: Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Otherwise, I think it's going to push us beyond November 1st. / Waleed Alasadi: Fine. Okay.
items.note: Internal Jumpr discussion (Waleed and Kobi only); not client-confirmed. Waleed's 'Fine. Okay.' is internal acceptance; client acceptance of the deferral is not shown.

items.topic: Redeposit import needed for manual overrides
items.statement: Kobi said the import process must be built anyway to support manual overrides.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think the import process we still need to build that anyways for manual overrides. That's why I'm thinking this doesn't need to be V1.
items.note: Internal Jumpr discussion (Waleed and Kobi only); not client-confirmed.

items.topic: How client's reallocation tool works is unknown
items.statement: Kobi said he does not know enough about the client's reallocation logic to estimate the effort to move it to Salesforce. The tool is a web interface built for one of the client's managers and used for a couple of months; Emily, Lena and Joyce had not seen it before; it is unknown how it connects to the spreadsheets or whether AI is involved.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: My concern is I don't know enough about the inner workings of the logic that does the reallocation to be able to confidently say… / Kobi Kunasekaran: how much work and effort it's going to be to move it to Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: It's a full web interface that they're using. and this is the first time both Emily, Lena, and Joyce are actually looking at it too. So even they didn't know about this. we were on a meeting with one of their VMs that's been doing the reallocation and somebody else built this for him and they've been using it for a couple months. So it's still new. but it's not a prompt. / Kobi Kunasekaran: It's a full-on website where they have a couple fields. they put that in. It already appears to be connected to all the spreadsheets that they have. How? I don't know. Nobody knows there is an AI involved. The AI is the one that I'm assuming I actually don't know. It might not be, but just based off the UI,… / Waleed Alasadi: So it's no AI involved at all. / Kobi Kunasekaran: it looks like it's CL. No, but based off the UI, it looks like claw generated. So maybe it's not AI,…
items.asr_note: 'claw'/'CL' = Claude [ASR?]; 'VMs' possibly a role title as heard [ASR?]

items.topic: Focus on day-to-day UI before automation/AI
items.statement: Kobi said the current focus is a simple day-to-day user interface and the transition from sheets to Salesforce, with automations and AI added afterwards; Waleed said okay.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think the focus right now is the day-to-day user interface and what that looks like and making that simple, right? It is that transition from sheets through Salesforce and… / Waleed Alasadi: Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: then yeah let's add all the automations that we can afterwards or all the AI I launching the plan afterwards.
